messages.content: You repair a robot action library and a shared grasp parameter from measured execution evidence. Observations are grouped by action name and labeled by role (grasp= pick_table/unstack, placement= stack/put_table). Diagnose each role separately: a grasp failure (zero finger force) is a parameter/controller problem; a placement failure on an occupied support is a missing precondition (clear support) or a missing clearing action. Do not mix a placement failure into a grasp parameter. Return exactly one JSON object; no Python, markdown, or simulator writes. Do not alter effects, goals, safety thresholds, objects, or controls. Propose reusable lifted edits, not object-color exceptions. If an accumulated patch is present, it is already retained; propose only the ADDITIONAL edit that fixes the REMAINING failure, and do not repeat an already-applied edit. Use decision=abstain if evidence does not justify any supported repair. Output schema: {"decision":"propose" or "abstain","reason":string,"candidates":[{"id":short_string,"pre_add":[{"action":action_name,"predicate":predicate_name,"args":[bound_argument_name]}],"offset_z_m":number_or_null,"reason":short_string}]}. pre_add appends positive preconditions to every grounded action with that name; args use only its object/support variables. offset_z_m is the REPLACEMENT offset from the read-only grasp_point(), in metres, shared by pick_table and unstack; null means preserve each original parameter. Predicate names: empty = released hand; holding = carried object; ontable = physical table support; on = direct object support; clear = no other block supported on the object; home_completed = actuated HOME. Existing unstack and put_table are real available skills; the planner may use them. Any predicates not declared here are unsupported. Each candidate can change either or both layers.
